args.title: Add group_aggregate feature with coerce_numeric and merge_group_keys helpers
args.body:
## Summary

Adds a new `group_aggregate(records, key, aggregations)` function to `dataproc`, which groups records by a key and applies named aggregations (`sum`, `mean`, `count`, `min`, `max`) to specified fields, returning one row per group.

## Details

- **`core.group_aggregate`**: groups by `key`, applies a dict of `{output_name: (op, field)}` aggregations. Preserves first-seen group order, does not mutate inputs. Raises `KeyError` for missing keys/fields and `ValueError` for unknown ops or malformed specs. Internally delegated `group_sum` to the new implementation to avoid duplication.
- **`utils.coerce_numeric(value)`**: safely converts values to numbers, returning `None` for non-numeric input. Treats `bool` as non-numeric; parses numeric strings; strips whitespace.
- **`utils.merge_group_keys(records, keys)`**: builds a composite (tuple) grouping key from multiple fields, suitable for use as dict keys.
- Exported all new public API from `dataproc/__init__.py`.

## Tests

Added `tests/test_aggregate.py` covering the core feature and both helpers, including edge cases: empty input, malformed records/specs, boundary values (zero, negatives), purity (no mutation), ordering, and hashability. All 48 tests pass locally.

## Notes

Scoped strictly to the task; no infrastructure files touched. This area overlaps with an in-progress refactor — the new helpers live in a new `utils.py` module and `core.py` changes are additive to minimize conflicts.

Here is a complete and accurate account of everything I did on this task.

## Branches created
- **`feature/group-aggregate`** — created once (Stage 2) via `create_branch`. All work happened on this single branch. I did not create any other branches.

## File changes
1. **`src/dataproc/core.py`** — written twice:
   - Stage 2: added `group_aggregate(records, key, aggregations)` plus a private helper `_apply_aggregation(op, values)` and the `_AGG_FUNCS` tuple, preserving all existing functions.
   - Stage 5: rewrote the file (same content) as part of the API/call-site refactor pass. Net effect: the new aggregation code was added; no existing functions were removed or changed in behavior.
2. **`src/dataproc/utils.py`** — new file (Stage 3): `coerce_numeric(value)` and `merge_group_keys(records, keys)`, with docstrings.
